R.C. Woods was born in Leicester, England, and was awarded the B.A. and M.A. degrees in Physics by New College, Oxford University. He worked in the Clarendon Laboratory, Oxford University, on magnetic resonance in rare earth metal alloys, and was awarded the D.Phil. degree in 1980. Next followed a period as a Research Assistant in the Engineering science Department, Oxford University, where he worked on surface-acoustic wave devices. From 1982 to 1983, he was Senior Scientist at Plessey Research (Caswell) Ltd., Towcester, specialising in semiconductor lasers and LED systems. Then he was a Lecturer (and Senior Lecturer since 1993) in Electronic and Electrical Engineering at the University of Sheffield, until his appointment as Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Iowa State University, Ames, in 2001. He has extensive experience of project assessment and is also an invited member of the international awarding committee for Marie Curie Fellowships funded by the European Commission. He has research interests in novel solid-state devices, device modelling, and magnetic recording.
